WHY THESE THREE

Both gates had to hold on the same morning, on the last completed session.

1 · TREND — 20-day average above the 50-day, price above both, and volume at least 50% of the name’s own 20-day average.

2 · STRUCTURE — higher highs and higher lows, with an area of interest — a price band the market has reacted at 3 or more times — sitting beneath price to stop under.

Of ~70 names, the 3 with the strongest 20-day momentum that clear both. TOUCHES is how many times that band has been defended; STOP is where the trail starts — just under the band, ceilinged at 12%.

A target is a candidate, not a position. The bot buys only if price breaks the trigger between 09:35 and 15:45 ET. Most days it buys nothing.

WHAT THIS DOES TO YOUR TRADES

Nothing. Not one of these gates an entry. They are on screen as weather, not as a rule.

All twenty were walk-forwarded as entry gates on the fused rule (regime_test.py). The last column is the share of 2,000 bootstrap histories in which gating on that signal beat not gating — the bar is 90%.

1 of 20 cleared. Testing twenty candidates at a 10% false-positive rate throws up 2.0 winners by chance, so one winner is fewer than chance predicts. XLU/SPY at 92.5% is what a lottery ticket looks like, and after correcting for twenty tests the bar is ~99.5%. None was adopted.

The bot’s own edge sits in 2018, 2020 and 2022 — exactly when SPY is under its long average. A regime gate deletes its best years and re-enters late. A filter that helps a dip-buyer hurts a breakout bot.

WHAT THE SENTIMENT NUMBER IS WORTH

The score is a lexicon reading of the headline. It is not a forecast, and there is no probability-of-rising on this page because one cannot honestly be computed.

Measured over 128,304 headlines and 30,361 symbol-days (2021–2026, entry at the open after each article, so nothing leaks backwards):

Every band sits on the base rate. Bull minus bear is +0.02 points, t = +0.28, permutation p = 0.372. At five days the spread is the wrong sign.

What IS estimable is distance, not direction: mean absolute move is 1.7% at a day, 4.6% at a week, 9.7% at a month. Also note Alpaca serves one publisher — 600 of 600 sampled articles were Benzinga — so this is a null result on one wire, not on news itself.
